build.reason: The recipe compiles the parser and target, then links their objects; the called string API is declared and defined.

input.reason: The entry accepts finite inputs of 8–512 bytes, copies them into terminated storage, and the string reader can pass their lines to the parser.

lifecycle.reason: The target checks allocation, keeps the copied input and static user object alive during the synchronous parse call, then frees the copy.

control_flow.reason: The entry calls ini_parse_string with a handler that returns success; name-only lines reach the changed else branch. The configuration exclusion for the guarded callback is assessed separately as a blocker.

accepted.requirement: Build this parser with INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE=1 so a name-only line after a prior parse error can execute the changed guarded handler path.
accepted.target_route: For an accepted input such as "[broken\nname\n", the entry calls ini_parse_string, which delegates through ini_parse_string_length to ini_parse_stream. The unterminated section records an error; the later name-only line requires the guarded handler path.
accepted.failure_condition: The target’s recipe supplies no enabling definition, so ini.h defaults INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE to 0 and compilation excludes the changed handler guard. No fuzzer input can enable that preprocessor branch.
accepted.alternative_paths: The target has one parse call and no configuration or alias that enables the branch. The default #else path records an error rather than calling the name-only handler; the fixture’s presence in the seed corpus does not change the compiled option.
